fullPassage: Patents grant inventors exclusive rights to their inventions for a certain period, allowing them the potential to profit from their creations. This can spur innovation by encouraging companies and individuals to share their technologies in return for a financial reward. But since an excessive number of patents have already been issued, and they cover overly minor aspects of a technology —keeping a tight rein on the components and minutiae that could form a whole greater than the sum of its parts— problems often arise when a company attempts to develop a new technology based on existing patents. For instance, in the smartphone industry, nearly every aspect of a smartphone, from screen size to scrolling features, is protected by a separate patent. For a company trying to design a new smartphone, this means that it has to pay licensing fees or pursue legal action to avoid violating the patents. As a result, less time and resources end up being directed towards the new technology. In essence, each patent is a tollgate on a highway.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: are protected → is protected (주어 every aspect가 단수라 단수동사 is)
det.analysis:
① grant ✅ 적절 — 주어 Patents(복수)에 맞는 복수동사
② arise ✅ 적절 — 주어 problems(복수)에 맞는 복수동사
③ are protected ❌ 오류 — 주어가 'nearly every aspect(거의 모든 부분)'인데, every로 시작하는 주어는 하나하나를 가리켜 단수 취급해요. 그래서 단수동사 is protected가 맞아요. 중간에 낀 'of a smartphone, from screen size to scrolling features'에 속으면 안 돼요 ←정답
④ pursue ✅ 적절 — 'has to pay ... or pursue'로 앞의 pay와 짝을 이루는 동사원형
det.tip: every + 명사 = 단수 취급 → 단수동사(is). 주어와 동사 사이의 긴 수식어에 속지 말기

questions.passage: Patents grant inventors exclusive rights to their inventions for a certain period, allowing them the potential to profit from their creations. This can spur innovation by encouraging companies and individuals to share their technologies in return for a financial reward. But since an excessive number of patents have already been issued, and they cover overly minor aspects of a technology —keeping a tight rein on the components and minutiae that could form a whole greater than the sum of its parts— problems often arise when a company attempts to develop a new technology based on existing patents. For instance, in the smartphone industry, nearly every aspect of a smartphone, from screen size to scrolling features, is protected by a separate patent. For a company trying to design a new smartphone, this means that it has to pay licensing fees or pursue legal action to avoid violating the patents. As a result, less time and resources end up being directed towards the new technology. In essence, each patent is a tollgate on a highway.

det.korean: have already been + 과거분사(수동): issue → issued
det.analysis:
빈칸 앞에 'have already been(현재완료 + been)'이 있어요. 특허는 사람에 의해 '발급되는' 대상이므로 수동태가 필요해요. 수동태는 be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.)이고, 여기서는 been 뒤에 과거분사가 와야 하므로 issue → issued로 바꿔요
→ have already been issued(이미 발급되어 왔다)
동사원형 issue를 그대로 두면 수동태가 완성되지 않아 틀려요
det.tip: have been + 과거분사 = ~되어 왔다(현재완료 수동). issue → issued
